messages:
meera: heads up — hosted p99 in us-west-2 spiked ~2.3x around 09:12 PDT. p95 up ~1.4x. dashboard shows short, repeated bursts in queue depth. noticed after a config roll for rate shaping on Skyline tenant. anyone on call?
alex: on it. i see queue depth jump from ~30->240 for a few seconds, then rapid fall. looks like burst shaping admitted many small concurrent requests rather than smoothing them.
tim: curious — profiling shows kernel-selector moving to aux kernels during those windows. aux kernels are slower for longer sequences we hit. probable mispick because batches got fragmented.
ryan: also seeing KV cache thrash. skyline traffic has lots of similar prefixes but different suffixes, cache hit% dropped from 78%->31% during spike.
julia: that cache drop would increase token compute time and increase latency — fits.
meera: timeline: 09:10 deploy of rate-shaper v2 (change: lower burst token cap, higher concurrency window). 09:12 latency spike. 09:16 rollback to v1, p99 back to baseline by 09:18.
infra-bot: deploy_handler: rollout completed for skyline/rate-shaper v2 at 2025-11-03T09:10:07Z by deploy-bot
alex: repro plan: run synthetic burst with skyline-like prefix/suffix mix. want to capture scheduler decisions + kernel selection traces.
tim: from flameprof output during spike (short):
```
flame %token-time
kernel_select  42%
attention_kern  28%
kv_lookup      15%
scheduler_wait 9%
other          6%
```
that kernel_select number is huge — we keep re-evaluating kernels for tiny fragmented batches.
ryan: evidence in logs: repeated calls to kselector with slightly different seq_len and batch_size. sample lines:
`kselector: tenant=skyline seq=64 batch=3 chosen=aux latency_delta=+12%`
`kselector: tenant=skyline seq=12 batch=1 chosen=main latency_delta=+3%`
julia: hypothesis: rate-shaper v2 admitted many small parallel requests, causing batches to be small and heterogeneous; kselector toggled kernels suboptimally; kv cache priming lost because identical prefixes were not batched together.
meera: immediate mitigation: rollback already done. longer term: add hysteresis to kernel-selector (avoid switching kernels for N seconds for a tenant), and have rate-shaper prefer coalescing similar prefixes where possible.
alex: action items:
- alex/tim: add transient kernel hysteresis PR and unit tests (ETA EOD)
- ryan: add extra KV cache metrics (per-tenant hit/miss histograms) and alert when hit% drops >30pts (ETA next sprint)
- julia: run synthetic burst tests against staging with v2 config variations and capture kernel decisions (ETA tomorrow)
- ops-oncall: keep Skyline throttled to current rate until changes validated (:thumbsup:)
ops-oncall: acknowledged. throttling in place.
meera: logging: added an adhoc short-lived trace to capture kselector inputs for the next 24h on skyline — will delete after. if anyone needs the trace id ping me.
alex: follow-up — creating perf ticket: PERF-1428, include flamegraphs + sample logs + replay script.
meera: thanks all. learnings: rate shaping that increases small concurrent inflight requests can backfire by fragmenting batches and provoking kernel misselection + KV cache thrash. prefer smoothing that increases batchability over pure concurrency for seqy workloads.
